I will use what is default, as long as I get to define the defaults. With Gentoo, I'll happily use OpenRC and have a separate boot partition. With Devuan, it's obviously SysVInit+startpar+insserv. A separate home partition is de rigeur. For wireless LAN wicd is my default.

I don't pick a distro for the interface it provides, I'll shun a distro for the interfaces it doesn't provide.

I'll change all the fonts. I'll customize the colours. I'll change the keyboard shortcuts for the functions I use to my defaults. (Hyper+q closes a window, Alt+Space launches dmenu or krunner, your CAPSLOCK is my compositing key, and so on.) Most importantly, I'll edit my bashrc, zshrc, and profile, and set -o vi.

clang is my default compiler.

I'll also block gtk3 and systemd at the system level, and facebook.com from the DNS cache. (which is unbound, simply because I know it from FreeBSD). And I'll have a web caching proxy on my machine, because browsers are stupid as a rule.
